full_judgment:
5. The defendant No. 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations and contending inter alia that the suit was not maintainable, barred by limitation and res-judicata and that the defendants case in short was that the Lal Mia sold the suit land to Suruj Mia by registered kabala dated 18-12-1944 and delivered possession of the suit land to him and that Suruj Mia had no son and he executed a registered a wasiatnama on 29-09-1975 in favour of his only daughter the defendant No. 2 i.e. Josthna Begum in respect of the suit land and since then she had been possessing the suit land and the plaintiffs earlier filed Title Suit No. 105 of 1977 in the 3rd Munsif Court, Comilla but they did not mention in that suit about the mortgage as such the suit was barred by res-judicata and that said suit was dismissed up to the High Court and that the mortgaged agreement dated 04-12-1947 was forged and fraudulent and that the suit was liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 8. Mr. Tafazzal Hossain, the learned advocate for the petitioners submitted that the courts below committed gross illegality in passing their judgments and decrees to the effect that during the continuance of 1st mortgage the suit land was given on 2nd mortgage at an enhanced money and the courts below ought to have allowed the 2nd mortgage which no courts below did. He further submitted that both the courts below committed illegality in putting the present suit under law of res judicata though the earlier suit for declaration of title and khash possession and the present one for redemption of mortgage and thus committed an error of law that occasioned a failure of justice. He again submitted that both the courts below failed to consider the evidence both oral and documentary in their true perspectives and also misunderstood the municipal law that the mortgage could be redeemed within 60 years of refusal and section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was not applicable in the present suit. He finally submitted that any registered documents of more than 30 years had the presumptive value, which was not considered by either of the courts below though the agreement was made on 04-12-1947. In support of his contention he cited the decision in the case of Sachindra Lal Das and others —Vs-Hriday Ranjan Das being his heirs Bimal Kanti Das and others, reported in 40 DLR(AD)56.
